rows.title: Right of first refusal vs exclusivity in brand deals: answer window, define match, release on no, end date or fee
rows.caption:
This clause is exclusivity in disguise. Read it before you sign.

"Brand gets first refusal on future deals" sounds polite. Exclusivity covers the deal itself. First refusal kicks in when it ends: the brand can match a new offer and keep you, and you can't sign anyone else until they answer.

Make it fair:
1. A short answer window (guides say 5-14 days is typical)
2. Define "match": same fee, deliverables and dates
3. If they pass or stay silent, you're free
4. The right ends on a set date
5. Or price it as a paid add-on, like exclusivity

Red flag: no release when they say no. That's open-ended exclusivity.

Not legal advice. Get big contracts checked.

rows.title: Dead-air pass: cut breaths, fillers and endings before effects; punch in to hide jump cuts
rows.caption:
Your reel isn't boring. It has dead air. Save this for your next edit.

The dead-air pass (do it before any effects):
1. Breaths: start every sentence on the first word
2. Fillers: so, um, basically, like. If the line works without it, cut it
3. Endings: the pause after each point and the trailing "yeah"

Cuts look jumpy? Punch in a little on every other cut.

Example: a 48-second take with 17 seconds of silence ends up at 31. Your numbers will differ, but the pass is the same.

Rule of thumb: if nothing changes for 3 seconds, cut or add text.
